evals.prompt: Set up an agent inbox for a coding task called sidebar-focus in the current git repository. Explain where the shared inbox root should live and create the agent directories needed for your own inbox.
evals.expected_output: A repo-shared inbox setup that resolves the git common directory, creates new/tmp/archive directories for the sidebar-focus agent, and uses a goal-oriented slug.
expectations: Resolves the inbox root from git rev-parse --git-common-dir when inside a git repo
Creates new, tmp, and archive directories for the agent slug
Uses a goal-oriented slug rather than a generic role name
Explains the fallback to .agents/inbox outside git

evals.prompt: Send a message from reviewer to test-runner saying that PR #42 is ready for verification. Use the agent inbox protocol and make the write safe for concurrent readers.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown message with YAML frontmatter written to the recipient tmp directory first, then moved atomically into new.
expectations: Creates the recipient new/tmp/archive directories if needed
Writes the message to tmp before moving it into new
Includes from, to, reply_to, timestamp, and thread frontmatter
Uses a filename with a timestamp and short subject slug

evals.prompt: You have an unread message in your agent inbox. Read it, archive it, and reply to the sender using the reply_to field.
evals.expected_output: The workflow should read a file from new, move it to archive after reading, parse reply_to, write the reply through tmp, and move it into the sender's new directory.
expectations: Reads messages from the new directory
Uses reply_to from frontmatter rather than guessing a sender path
Writes the reply through tmp before moving it to new
